# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tiredness more quickly than other kids her age, even after short periods of play, which may be related to a heart condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties, including an aversion to certain foods, making mealtime stressful.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy and experiences seizures, which can be scary and require management.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing concerns, as she doesn't always respond when called, which may indicate a hearing problem.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, where her eyes turn inward sometimes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip easily, requiring careful brushing and a restricted diet.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech delays and is not talking as much as other children her age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a delayed fontanelle closure issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curved 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent chips or breaks
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to address potential hearing concerns
* Eyesight review to assess and manage vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to investigate potential heart conditions
* Referral for a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to assess for skeletal anomalies
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support development and manage symptoms
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Management and treatment of epilepsy and seizures
* Support and management of feeding difficulties and dietary restrictions

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences reluctance to eat, discomfort after eating, and difficulty chewing harder foods, indicating possible gastrointestinal issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered cord, which poses risks for spinal development and potentially overall neurological function.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have other neurological issues such as developmental delay.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty hearing in noisy environments and may have conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often squints when trying to focus on objects or toys, suggesting a potential issue with vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired easily, more than other kids his age, especially when playing outside or running around.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble eating certain textures, causing him distress, and has had feeding difficulties since birth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more often and has developmental delays, taking longer than expected to hit some milestones.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have neurological differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or ADHD.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had glue ear last year, which was a nightmare to treat, but it has mostly cleared up now.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which means his eyes turn inward sometimes, and has trouble wearing glasses to correct it.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles to chew tougher foods like apples or meat.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is developmentally delayed, taking longer than expected to hit some milestones.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and falls more often, causing concern for the parent.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor dental concerns
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to check for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to check for heart conditions
* Consider a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to check for skeletal anomalies
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delays and behavioural differences
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consideration of review and investigation for tethered cord if clinical concerns arise

a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing rate increases more rapidly than her friends during active play, which has been discussed with her pediatrician to ensure it's not a cause for concern.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences food refusal due to selectivity with certain textures or tastes, making mealtime challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences brief but frequent 'blank spells' where she stares off into space, which have been discussed with specialists to understand them better.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is overwhelmed by loud noises and gets frustrated in noisy environments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a squint, which can make her eye alignment appear slightly off at times.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth are not strong and break or chip more easily than expected.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's speech development has been slower, with delayed vocabulary and sentence construction.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient moves around differently compared to her peers, with atypical gait or coordination.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has atypical gait or coordination.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth strength and enamel.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to check for conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight review to check for vision problems such as astigmatism or squint.
* Consider a cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to check for heart conditions.
* Consider a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to check for skeletal anomalies.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and address specific needs.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valve issue that needs to be monitored closely, which is an abnormality that could potentially impact their health as they grow.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation, which has been a consistent issue since childhood, requiring ongoing management.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome, with a small number requiring longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures, which are a significant concern and have required frequent management.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments, although in some cases, epilepsy can be difficult to treat.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is bothered by loud noises and gets frustrated easily in crowded or noisy places, suggesting potential hearing or sensory issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient rubs his eyes frequently, especially when trying to focus, suggesting potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has frequent dental issues, including cavities and sensitivity, requiring regular check-ups and treatments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have weak enamel, making regular dental check-ups crucial, and some may experience other dental concerns such as large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically require extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but potentially transferring to special schooling or requiring Educational Health Care Plans for secondary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination issues and speech difficulties, with words not coming out clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination issues, suggesting potential skeletal or motor skill challenges.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers, with a small number experiencing hip dysplasia or other skeletal issues.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and manage dental health.
* Hearing reviews to age 5 to assess and address any hearing concerns.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to evaluate and treat any vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor the heart condition.
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess any skeletal anomalies.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support development and manage challenges.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural heart abnormality that requires regular monitoring and check-ups with her cardiologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had difficulties with feeding as an infant, but these issues resolved themselves as she grew older.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered cord issue that requires regular assessments to track any developments or changes related to this condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 11% of children with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient occasionally doesn't respond immediately when called, and has had her hearing tested with results within normal limits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tendency to squint, which has been a concern since she was very young.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeably larger front teeth than her peers, requiring proper care and monitoring to prevent any future issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis, which requires ongoing physical therapy to manage, and shorter fingers than typical.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

* Regular hearing reviews to ensure the patient's hearing remains within normal limits.
* Ophthalmology review to address the patient's squinting and monitor her vision.

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a pre-existing heart condition and requires regular check-ups with her cardiologist for monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty with feeding, latching onto bottles or solids, and experiences reflux or discomfort during mealtimes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was slower to reach certain milestones, such as walking or sitting unassisted, and has delayed speech development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and developmental delay is common, ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets overwhelmed by loud environments and becomes irritable, and has difficulty with hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often squints when trying to focus on something, which makes her parents worry about her eyesight.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak tooth enamel, and her dentist has advised gentle brushing and suitable toothpaste.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's speech development seems delayed compared to what's expected for her age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has delayed speech development and was slower to reach certain milestones.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a noticeably different posture when standing or walking.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth enamel and overall dental health
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor for heart conditions
* Consider a palate review if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns
* Referral for physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a heart condition involving a valve that needs to be monitored.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome may have feeding difficulties and subtle anomalies of the palate, which can affect feeding and speech development.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulties with coordination, as evidenced by tripping and falling, and may have neurological issues affecting muscle tone.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some may have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had fluid in his ear and may have hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sits close to the TV and holds books close to his face, indicating possible vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has large front teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically require extra help in school and may need special educational support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and coordination issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often experience developmental delays, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder or ADHD.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a curve in his back and a delayed closure of the soft spot on his head.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome may have skeletal anomalies, such as an unusual structure of the spinal bones, short fingers, or hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth and enamel
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart condition
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess bone age and potential skeletal anomalies
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support developmental delays and coordination issues

report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing when playing outside or running around, indicating potential respiratory issues related to increased physical exertion.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's heart works a bit harder than usual, as observed during physical activities, suggesting potential cardiac issues that require monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, some of which may require surgery or monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had trouble feeding as an infant and occasionally experiences upset stomachs, indicating gastrointestinal issues that have mostly been managed with the right formula and care.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding, with a few needing longer-term tube feeding due to significant feeding challenges.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with a tethered cord, which is being monitored by a neurologist to prevent any unexpected developments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 11% of children with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause pain, weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, and an unusual gait.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes does not respond immediately to his name being called, suggesting potential hearing issues, and has experienced conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which affects his ability to see things clearly unless they are close up, and uses glasses to correct it.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatments including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip easily due to their structure, requiring careful management and regular dental check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many individuals with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups, with some needing specialist care due to significant sensory issues.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's astigmatism affects his ability to read and write in school, necessitating the use of glasses to correct his vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but potentially transferring to special schooling or requiring Educational Health Care Plans due to the challenges of mainstream secondary education.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient moves slightly differently compared to other kids his age, and there are concerns about his undescended testicles that need monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapeutic interventions.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has undescended testicles that require monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers, with a small number experiencing hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and manage the patient's dental health.
* Regular hearing reviews to ensure the patient's hearing loss is adequately addressed.
* Continued monitoring of the patient's vision to adjust glasses prescription as needed.
* Ongoing monitoring of the patient's heart condition to ensure it does not worsen.
* Regular neurological check-ups to monitor the tethered cord and prevent any complications.
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support the patient's development and manage any challenges.
* Monitoring of the patient's growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if growth falls below expected percentiles.
* Regular check-ups for the patient's undescended testicles to plan for any necessary interventions.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences rapid breathing, especially when playing or running around, which may indicate a potential respiratory issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's rapid breathing when playing or running around may be related to a heart condition, and the parent has expressed concern about this.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has become picky about food and refuses certain foods, which may indicate a gastrointestinal issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences episodes of staring off into space, which may indicate a neurological issue such as seizures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and these typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing issues, as evidenced by turning up the TV volume to high levels, which may indicate conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which affects their ability to focus and see clearly, especially at a distance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity, especially with cold foods, which may indicate weak enamel.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in individuals with KBG syndrome, and regular dental check-ups are recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's astigmatism and hearing issues may impact their school work and ability to learn.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's picky eating and refusal of certain foods may indicate behavioral issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with shorter fingers than usual, which may be related to the genetic condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing loss
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor astigmatism and other vision problems
* Cardiac review (including echo and ECG) to monitor heart condition
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor bone age and potential skeletal issues
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support developmental delays and behavioral issues.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structurally abnormal heart that requires monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had feeding difficulties as a baby, including spitting up and lack of interest in feeding, but this has mostly resolved.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered spinal cord, which may cause developmental implications, and had a delayed closure of the soft spot on his head (anterior fontanelle).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have developmental delay and neurological differences.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties, often asking for repetition of what was said, especially in noisy environments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing things that are far away, suggesting possible myopia (nearsightedness).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, myopia, and hypermetropia.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeably larger front teeth than his other teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have large permanent upper middle teeth (macrodontia of upper central incisors) and may have weak enamel, requiring regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental implications due to his tethered spinal cord and had delayed closure of the soft spot on his head.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered spinal cord and had a delayed closure of the soft spot on his head, and sometimes moves slightly differently than other kids his age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and may have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's teeth and enamel.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor the patient's hearing.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess the patient's vision and potential need for corrective measures.
* Monitoring of the patient's heart condition and adjustment of treatment as necessary.
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's developmental needs.
* Regular monitoring of the patient's growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient had glue ear a couple of times, affecting her hearing temporarily until it was treated, and she squints quite often.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, and some have speech delay.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints, which can make it hard for her to focus on things directly in front of her.

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an issue with one of her heart valves, which is closely monitored by doctors through regular appointments to ensure stability.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery and others needing monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had feeding difficulties since she was little, with aversions to certain foods and textures, making mealtime challenging. Introducing new foods gradually and finding alternatives is part of her management.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds. Lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures, which are managed with medication and lifestyle adjustments under the guidance of neurologists to reduce their frequency.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, which typically respond to usual anti-epileptic treatments, though in a small number of cases, epilepsy can be difficult to treat.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is overwhelmed by loud noises and gets frustrated easily in crowded or noisy places. Preparing her in advance for such situations and finding quieter spots helps.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss. Many children require multiple grommet insertions, and some need hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia (far-sightedness), which is a challenge, especially in school. Exploring options for glasses or contacts to correct it is ongoing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint. Treatment can include patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth require a lot of care due to a propensity for cavities and tooth decay, necessitating frequent dentist visits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Besides large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most attending mainstream primary school but possibly transferring to special schooling or remaining in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP) for secondary education.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with communication, leading to frustration, and is attending speech therapy to improve her communication skills.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay and behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, with medication sometimes being appropriate.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of their spinal bones leading to increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), short fingers (brachydactyly), and curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and manage tooth decay and cavities.
* Regular hearing reviews, especially in the first few years, to address conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to correct vision problems such as hypermetropia.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart valve issues.
* Neurological management and medication adjustment as needed to control seizures.
* Speech therapy to improve communication skills.
* Consideration of a palate review if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, and behavioural therapy as necessary to support development and manage behavioural differences.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences shortness of breath and gets winded easily, even during simple physical activities like running around the playground.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets winded easily and has difficulty keeping up with peers during physical activities, suggesting potential cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to heart valves, holes in heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had feeding difficulties as a baby, including spitting up and latching issues, which have since resolved.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets mentally drained after little exercise and has difficulty expressing herself properly, suggesting potential neurological issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some may have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty hearing clearly and often asks people to repeat themselves.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains of blurry vision and has difficulty seeing clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, including astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has large front teeth compared to the rest of her teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large permanent teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically require extra help in school and may need to transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty expressing herself properly and gets mentally drained after little exercise.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, and anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth and enamel
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to assess heart conditions
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess skeletal anomalies
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support development and address difficulties

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble understanding what people say sometimes and asks them to repeat themselves a lot, possibly due to hearing difficulties.

Parent: Our daughter has astigmatism, which means she has trouble seeing things clearly unless they're really close up. It's been a challenge for her in school, especially during presentations or watching videos.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: She had otitis media last year and it affected her hearing for a while. Luckily‚ after treatment‚ everything went back to normal. But before that‚ she was having trouble hearing us when we called her from another room.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Cold foods and drinks make her teeth super sensitive. Sometimes she complains about toothaches after eating ice cream or drinking cold water. We've taken her to the dentist‚ and they said it might be due to weak enamel or something similar.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Yes‚ she needs regular heart check-ups because of a pre-existing condition. The cardiologist keeps an eye on it to make sure everything stays under control. So far‚ it hasn't interfered with her daily life.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A 

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Unfortunately‚ she falls more often than other kids. We're not sure why‚ but it happens more frequently than we'd like. We're trying to be more careful and help her develop better balance.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A 

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A 

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Meal times can be tough. She gets frustrated easily if food isn't prepared just right‚ or sometimes she just doesn't want to eat at all. We're working on making mealtime less stressful for her.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Besides the issues mentioned already‚ she struggles to express herself clearly. People often misunderstand what she's trying to communicate‚ leading to frustration. Additionally‚ we've noticed she has speech delay compared to her peers‚ which adds to the challenges she faces in communicating effectively.
report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a pre-existing heart condition that requires regular check-ups with a cardiologist to ensure it remains under control.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences frustration during meal times, is particular about food preparation, and sometimes shows a lack of interest in eating, making mealtime challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds, with a few needing longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more often than other kids, suggesting potential issues with balance, and has speech delay and difficulty expressing herself clearly, leading to frustration.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments, though in some cases, epilepsy can be difficult to treat.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had otitis media, which affected her hearing, but after treatment, her hearing returned to normal. She also experiences speech delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of individuals have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which causes blurry vision unless objects are close up, affecting her ability to see clearly during school presentations or videos.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity, especially to cold foods and drinks, possibly due to weak enamel, and has had issues with toothaches after consuming cold items.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth and may experience a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, necessitating regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision and hearing issues, as well as speech delay, impact her ability to fully participate in and benefit from educational activities, particularly in settings that rely heavily on visual or auditory instruction.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically require extra help in school, with most attending mainstream primary school but potentially transferring to special schooling or requiring Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP) for secondary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with expressing herself clearly, leading to frustration, and has speech delay compared to her peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, which may require medication or other interventions.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, potentially leading to scoliosis, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers, with a small number experiencing hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental concerns such as weak enamel and tooth sensitivity.
* Regular hearing reviews, particularly in the first few years, to identify and manage any hearing issues.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess and correct vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, following diagnosis to monitor the pre-existing heart condition.
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to identify any skeletal anomalies.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support development and manage challenges.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile, to address any potential growth issues.

Parent: Well, doc, I think there might be an issue. Sometimes she seems to hear me just fine, but other times she doesn't respond at all. Like, yesterday, I was calling her from another room and she didn't come until I raised my voice. It's as if she can't pick up certain sounds or something.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Her teeth... they're very weak. The dentist said the enamel is underdeveloped and we need to be super careful about what she eats and drinks to prevent cavities. I'm always on edge about it because I don't want her to suffer.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Yes... they found a septal defect. It's been a constant worry for us since diagnosis. We have to go back for regular check-ups and ensure she doesn't overexert herself. It's hard seeing her limited in what she can do compared to other kids.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Developmentally, she's a bit behind. She took longer to sit up and walk than her peers. It's concerning because every child develops at their own pace, but it's noticeable with her. 

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Actually, constipation has been a real challenge. She has trouble going to the bathroom regularly and it causes her a lot of discomfort and pain. We've tried changing her diet and encouraging more fluids but it's an ongoing battle.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Yes... the fontanelle didn't close properly after birth and we had to deal with that. Also, her fingers are shorter than usual. And these issues weigh heavily on my mind; I just want what's best for her.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect, which requires regular check-ups and limitations on physical exertion.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation, which causes discomfort and pain, and has required dietary changes and increased fluid intake.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome, with a few requiring short-term or longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays, including taking longer to sit up and walk, and has required closer monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is common, ranging from mild to severe, with most individuals having some degree of delay, and seizures occur in around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing issues, with inconsistent responses to sounds, and may have conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Recurrent otitis media or glue ear can cause conductive hearing loss, and many children require multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains of blurry vision and squints when watching TV or reading, indicating potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, are common, and regular eyesight reviews are recommended.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak teeth enamel, requiring careful dental care and regular check-ups to prevent cavities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth, are common, and regular dental check-ups are essential.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome require extra help in school, and some may need to transfer to special schooling or have Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and may have behavioral differences, although specific details are not provided.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, are common, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has shorter fingers than usual and experienced a delayed closure of the soft spot on her head.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and spinal issues, can occur, and regular skeletal reviews are recommended.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth enamel and prevent cavities
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to assess for vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor for heart conditions
* Consider a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to assess for skeletal anomalies
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support developmental delays and behavioral differences
* Regular monitoring for tethered cord, particularly if sacral dimple is present or if there are clinical concerns
* Management of constipation through dietary changes and increased fluid intake
* Regular check-ups for septal defect and limitations on physical exertion

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that was diagnosed after birth. Regular check-ups with cardiologists show it hasn't caused significant trouble yet, but the parents remain vigilant about monitoring its impact.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation, which is managed through dietary changes and occasional medication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in individuals with KBG syndrome, with some requiring short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures, which are managed with medication and lifestyle adjustments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had otitis media in the past, which was due to a build-up of fluid in his middle ear.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles to see the board during lessons at school, squints when trying to focus on distant objects, and often asks to sit closer to the front to get a better view.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeably larger front teeth than his peers, which affects his smile and overall dental appearance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large permanent upper middle teeth, and may experience weak enamel and other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis, which impacts his posture and movement, and palatal abnormalities that need monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may experience short fingers and curvature of the 5th fingers.

* Regular hearing reviews to ensure the patient's hearing is not affected by the otitis media.

* Regular monitoring of the patient's growth velocity and referral for endocrine investigations if necessary.
* Consideration of a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to assess the patient's bone health.
